plan: In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding only risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $47, the optimal action is to bid exactly $47, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay the appropriate second-highest price if I win.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, bidding above my value risks overpaying, and bidding below risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to suggest collusion or irrational behavior, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my valuation of $33 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: since the price paid depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), overbidding risks paying more than my value, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' strategies, I should bid exactly my value of $36 to maximize expected profit.
